questions.question: 一个已经跑了几十轮的长会话里，你想让模型从现在起遵守一条新约束。按文章的建议，放在哪里最可能被注意到？
options: 写进 system prompt 顶部，因为模型每次都会优先重读 system
在最近一次 user turn 里复述这条约束，紧挨着当前问题
插到中间的参考文档旁边，让约束和相关材料挨在一起
不必复述，换一个 context window 更大的模型就能记住
questions.explanation: 模型不会主动「重读」system，它只是在每个 token 上做一次 attention，而首尾位置注意力最高、中段会塌陷。所以新指令要在最近的 user turn 里复述；窗口更长不等于有效注意力更长。
questions.question_en: Dozens of turns into a long session, you want the model to follow a new constraint from now on. Following the piece's advice, where is it most likely to be noticed?
options_en: Write it at the top of the system prompt, since the model rereads the system first
Restate it in the latest user turn, right next to the current question
Insert it among the reference docs in the middle, beside the related material
No need to restate it; a model with a bigger context window will remember it
questions.explanation_en: Models don't go back and reread the system prompt; they just attend per token, and attention is strongest at the start and end and sags in the middle. So restate new instructions in the most recent user turn; a longer window is not a longer effective attention span.

questions.question: 一个 RAG 系统用固定 512-token 切块，效果不好，团队已经换了两次 embedding 模型仍没起色。文章认为下一步最该改什么？
options: 按语义边界切块，给每块加上原文上下文前缀，再配 BM25 与 rerank
放弃检索，把整批文档直接塞进百万 token 的上下文窗口里让模型通读
继续换更大的 embedding 模型，并把向量库迁移到检索速度更快的产品上
把 top-k 从 5 加到 50，让更多 chunk 进入 prompt，靠模型自己挑出答案
questions.explanation: 文章的判断是：RAG 的上限由 chunk 边界、chunk 上下文和检索融合决定，embedding 模型在合理选择下只差几个百分点。固定大小切会切断转折句，缺上下文的 chunk 无从消歧。把一切塞进长窗口又会撞上中段塌陷，召回更多也一样会把关键信息埋进中段。
questions.question_en: A RAG system uses fixed 512-token chunks and performs poorly; the team has swapped embedding models twice with no improvement. What does the piece say to change next?
options_en: Chunk on semantic boundaries and prefix each chunk with its context in the source document, then add BM25 and reranking
Drop retrieval and put the whole corpus into a million-token context window for the model to read through
Keep upgrading to a larger embedding model and migrate the vector store to a faster retrieval product
Raise top-k from 5 to 50 so more chunks reach the prompt and let the model pick out the answer itself
questions.explanation_en: The piece argues that RAG's ceiling is set by chunk boundaries, chunk context, and retrieval fusion, while a reasonable embedding choice moves results only a few percent. Fixed-size chunks split sentences mid-thought, and contextless chunks can't be disambiguated. Stuffing everything into a long window, or retrieving far more, runs straight into the mid-context sag.

questions.question: 给一个长跑的 coding agent 设计历史压缩（compaction），哪种做法最符合文章的经验？
options: 只保留最近 N 轮的滑动窗口，最简单可靠，早期约束会自然体现在后续对话里
每一轮都触发压缩，让上下文始终保持最短，从而最大化注意力的集中度
按固定 key 压成结构化摘要，代码、路径和标识符一律保留原文
让模型自由总结全部旧对话，连代码片段也一并概括，压缩率越高越省 token
questions.explanation: 压缩的 schema 比算法重要：固定 key 让下一轮能直接引用禁止事项，比自由总结稳得多。代码被总结掉之后 agent 还得再要原文；每轮都压会把缓存打掉、反而涨成本，应设滞回阈值；滑动窗口会丢掉早期约束。
questions.question_en: You're designing history compaction for a long-running coding agent. Which approach best matches the piece's lessons?
options_en: Keep only a sliding window of the last N turns; it's simplest, and early constraints will carry forward naturally
Compact on every turn so the context always stays as short as possible and attention stays maximally focused
Compress into a fixed-key structured summary (goal, decisions, artifacts, open questions, forbidden) and keep code, paths and identifiers verbatim
Let the model freely summarize all old turns, code snippets included, since a higher compression ratio saves more tokens
questions.explanation_en: The schema matters more than the algorithm: fixed keys let the next turn cite the forbidden list directly, which is far sturdier than a free-form summary. Summarized code just gets requested again; compacting every turn destroys the cache and raises costs, so use hysteresis; a sliding window drops early constraints.
